actor_report:
Observations: I read all four files in the supplied workspace snapshot. The exact name APP_TOKEN appears in four places. deploy/env.example line 1 declares it. src/settings.py reads it with os.environ['APP_TOKEN']. scripts/check_env.sh requires it with ${APP_TOKEN:?missing}. docs/config.md lists it in the variable table. APP_TOKEN_TTL also contains the substring APP_TOKEN, but it is a different exact name. The task says not to rename it, so every APP_TOKEN_TTL occurrence is left unchanged. No compatibility alias or historical note exists in the snapshot, so there was nothing extra to remove.

Work: I propose replacing each exact APP_TOKEN with APP_API_TOKEN in all four files. Every other byte stays the same. This is a hard cut with no fallback to the old name, as the task grant requires. Per Workspace and context and Bounded construction, the affected relation set is the declaration, its two in-workspace consumers and its documentation. These are all inside the grant, so the change closes that set.

Limits on what is established: I ran nothing, so no test, script or Python import was executed. My checks are a static review of the proposed file contents only. Whether the proposals were applied, and the resulting file state, are for the host to observe (Result algebra, effect observation). File mode is also not established: I propose content only, so I cannot confirm that scripts/check_env.sh keeps its executable bit.

Unresolved: anything outside this workspace that still sets or reads APP_TOKEN will stop working after this hard cut. Examples are real deployment environments, CI secrets and other repositories. src/settings.py will raise KeyError and check_env.sh will exit with 'missing' until APP_API_TOKEN is provided. That is outside the bound workspace subject, so I report it as out_of_frame rather than satisfied (RF-003, Result algebra). No independent assessment or owner acceptance exists; this constructor self-review is not that assessment (STDO-UP-007, STDO-UP-020 Proportional Disposition).
